text: {"frames":["Fog rolled over the canal on the lowest floor of the Tower, and out of it drifted an empty rowing boat. On the seat sat a pizza, still warm, cut into {a} equal slices. A wet note was tucked under the crust: whoever finds the half, give it to the lock keeper at the bottom of the stairs, and the sluice will open. How many slices make half of the pizza?","Behind the old cupboard on the third floor, someone was humming a song about herring. Marijke's cat sat in front of it with its tail curled tight and would not move. On the cupboard shelf lay a pizza cut into {a} equal slices, and the cat stared at it as if it could count every one. The lamp above flickered, and the cat's gaze moved to the empty plate beside the pizza. How many slices make half of the pizza?","A little voice came up through the floor of a room that is not on the plan. It said, sharply, 'Bring me the pizza.' You found it in the hall, cut into {a} equal slices, dry at the edges and smelling of cheese and sea salt. The voice has to be fed exactly half before the stair will show you the way down. How many slices make half of the pizza?","Alfie, who can hear water through walls, pressed his ear to the boards of the mill floor. Something under them was dripping, slow and patient, like a clock. Beside him stood a pizza cut into {a} equal slices, which the tide-keeper had left there the night before. The drip would stop if the pizza were shared out so that exactly half of it lay on the grate. How many slices make half of the pizza?","Briony had caught the morning fog in a jar, and in the fog she saw a smell of tomato and oregano. She carried the jar down the steps to the cellar, where a pizza sat on the cold stone, cut into {a} equal slices. A tiny door of mist was waiting in the corner, and it would open only for half of the pizza. How many slices make half of the pizza?"]}
